description: Calculate the band gap of Mn-doped CeO2 (111) surface. Mn substitution at Ce site introduces Mn 3d mid-gap states and narrows the effective gap. PBE severely underestimates the gap.
user_prompt: Calculate the band gap of Mn-doped CeO2 (111) surface (cubic, Fm-3m), where one Ce atom at surface is substituted by Mn, and report its value in eV.

references: Cen, Liu, Wu, Wang & Weng, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 14, 5769-5777 (2012)
method.modeling: Use a CeO2(111) slab with one surface Ce atom substituted by Mn; the reference work used a 3x3x1 nine-layer slab with about 15 A vacuum.
method.rationale: The scored value is the 0.31 eV position relative to the Fermi level of the unfilled Mn 3d-O 2p gap state A reported by Cen et al. at Ueff(Mn 3d)=4.5 eV with Ueff(Ce 4f)=5.0 eV. The same work reports approximately 0.5 eV for the energy interval from the valence-band maximum (VBM) to this unoccupied dopant state in the Mn-substituted CeO2(111) slab; the retained 0.31 eV target is the Fermi-referenced state position. Cen et al. used PW91+U rather than PBE+U, so the wide absolute tolerance covers PW91/PBE differences, Mn oxidation-state initialization, O 2p hole localization, and slab/DOS sampling sensitivity.
